text.en:
In summer Salma's uncle sold mangoes in the weekly market. On the first day when there were few mangoes the price was high. A week later many sellers came with mangoes and the price fell.
"Prices change with how many mangoes there are and how many people want them," he said.

A market is a place or a system where buyers and sellers meet to exchange goods and services. It can be a weekly haat, a shop, a mall or an online website.
Demand is how much of a thing people want to buy and supply is how much sellers have to sell. When demand is high and supply is low, prices rise. When supply is high and demand is low, prices fall.
Consumers buy goods and should check quality, price and weight and ask for a bill. Consumers have rights such as safety and being informed. Wholesale markets sell in large quantities and retail markets sell to ordinary buyers.
A market is where buyers and sellers meet to exchange goods and services.
Demand is how much people want to buy. Supply is how much sellers have.
When demand is high and supply is low, prices rise.
Wholesale sells in bulk. Retail sells to ordinary buyers. Ask for a bill.

problem.en: Why does the price of tomatoes rise in a market when heavy rain damages the crop?

text.en: Heavy rain reduces the number of tomatoes, so supply falls.
People still want tomatoes, so demand stays.
Low supply with steady demand pushes the price up.

prompt.en: A friend says shopkeepers set prices only to cheat. How will you explain?

requiredIdeas.en: Prices also depend on supply, demand and the cost of goods.
As consumers we can compare and ask for a bill.

points.en: A market brings buyers and sellers together.
Consumers should check quality and ask for a bill.
